paper text.text:
Lemma~\ref{r1:matching-test} makes $B+ab+ac+ad+ae$ nonplanar
as well. Thus $\Psi_3\cup B$ fails both tests of
Lemma~\ref{r1:missing-a-criterion}, and minimality gives
$G=\Psi_3\cup B$.

The graph $H_2$ is a $K_5$-minor-free minor of $G$, so it contains
a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision. Apply Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision}
with attachments $b,c,d,e$ and added edges $bc,de$.
The reduction keeps the interior connected, all four attachments,
and $H_2$ nonplanar. The preceding argument therefore keeps both
tests failing, so minimality leaves $B$ unchanged.
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} gives $26{,}633$
possibilities for $B$. Each resulting graph $\Psi_3\cup B$
is toroidal, has a $K_5$ minor or a proper nontoroidal minor,
or is isomorphic to $\mathfrak T_{54}$~\supp{E23}.

vertex names: Psi_3: twins p, q with neighbourhood {a,b,c} and r, z with neighbourhood {a,d,e}, as in Section 6. Further vertices with neighbourhood {a,b,c} are p3, p4, and with {a,d,e} r3, r4. Interior vertices of bridges are u0, u1, ...

disjoint twin triples.meaning: Section 6 assumes any two twin triples share exactly one vertex
